parsed.summary: The Lean file states that some finitely presented group (in Type) is not sofic, with a bespoke definition of soficity for arbitrary groups. The definition matches the Gromov–Weiss notion. The excerpt only shows Theorem 1.1 (the unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra L_{F2}(1,2)× is not sofic), and nothing in it mentions finite presentation. So the target theorem is not visibly the paper's stated theorem.

glossary.plain: Normalized Hamming distance between two permutations of a finite set Y: the fraction of points y where p y ≠ q y.
A positive integer n together with a map G → Sym(n) sending 1 to the identity. It is not required to be a homomorphism.
glossary.standard_concept: Almost-action of G on a finite set
glossary.note: Only map_one is required, which is standard for sofic approximations.

glossary.plain: For g,h in F, d(σ(gh), σ(g)σ(h)) < ε. For g ≠ 1 in F, d(σ(g), id) > 1 − ε.
glossary.note: Multiplicativity and separation match the paper's description (multiplication holds almost everywhere, non-identity elements move almost every point). gh need not lie in F, which is fine.

glossary.plain: For every finite F ⊆ G and every ε in (0,1), there is a permutation model that is (F,ε)-good.
glossary.note: It is stated for arbitrary groups, not only countable ones. This agrees with the standard definition.

glossary.plain: There exist a group G in Type that is finitely presented (Mathlib's Group.IsFinitelyPresented) and not sofic.
glossary.standard_concept: Existence of a finitely presented non-sofic group
glossary.note: Mathlib's Group.IsFinitelyPresented is assumed to be the standard notion (not checked).

lean_claims.plain: There exists a group G (in Type 0) that is finitely presented and does not satisfy the sofic approximation property.

paper_claims.plain: The unit group L_{F2}(1,2)× of the binary Leavitt algebra is not sofic.

flags.explanation: The paper defines soficity for countable groups, while Lean's definition applies to any group. The two agree on countable groups, and the existential target uses a bespoke definition rather than a Mathlib one. The model action need not be multiplicative, and composition order (g∘h versus h∘g) is a convention that does not affect the notion.
flags.probe_idea: Prove that the Sofic definition is invariant under replacing action g with action g⁻¹ (the anti-homomorphism convention).
